ai_summary: Great Britain's total wind generation currently stands at 3.1 GW, with Scottish wind output providing an estimated 2.0 GW, which corresponds to 19.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This robust zero-carbon output anchors Scottish carbon intensity at an exemplary 0 gCO2/kWh, sharply outperforming the prevailing GB-wide figure of 220 gCO2/kWh. Nevertheless, transmission export constraints prevent this abundant green electricity from being fully utilized across the wider grid. Consequently, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 849 MWh through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring an immediate constraint cost of about £47,969. Because this clean generation could not reach southern demand, an estimated 161,329 m3 of fossil gas was burned elsewhere on the system to compensate, needlessly emitting 297 tonnes of CO2. Extrapolating today’s constraint spend implies an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £18 million. When socialized across annual national electricity demand, this adds an estimated £0.07/MWh to everybody's invoice in the UK, highlighting the ongoing financial and environmental penalties caused by existing transmission network bottlenecks.
